title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Following the Cash — 10-Year Financials, Working Capital & Earnings Quality
question: Do GNA Axles' 10-year financial statements prove genuine cash compounding, or do working-capital absorption and modest ROCE cap its intrinsic quality?

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion, cash flow is a fact, and return on capital employed is the final judge of both.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: Let us review the multi-year audited ledger from Screener consolidated statements [1]. From FY15 to FY26, GNA grew revenue from ₹430 Cr to ₹1,478 Cr. TTM sales through September 2026 hit ₹1,778 Cr [1]. Net Profit grew more than five-fold from ₹22 Cr to ₹117 Cr, reaching ₹145 Cr TTM [1]. Two P&L facts stand out. First, OPM% never fell below 13% in any year of the decade. Second, depreciation nearly tripled from ₹23 Cr (FY15) to ₹70 Cr (FY26) as GNA reinvested in presses and CNCs, while interest stayed low at ₹7–14 Cr [1].

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY15–TTM, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Consistent 13%–16% OPM across a full decade of freight and tractor cycles, with H1 FY27 driving TTM sales to a record ₹1,778 Cr and TTM PAT to ₹145 Cr [1].

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Fortification & Zero-Dilution Equity Growth

web_blocks.html: GNA's balance sheet is its quietest strength. Total Reserves grew nearly ten-fold from ₹98 Cr (FY15) to ₹1,031 Cr (September 2026), lifting total equity to ₹1,074 Cr [1]. Equity Capital rose from ₹21 Cr in FY23 to ₹43 Cr in FY24 via a 1:1 bonus share issue. That doubled the share count to 4.29 Cr shares with zero dilutive equity raises [1][25]. Borrowings stood at ₹203 Cr in September 2026, down from ₹259 Cr in March 2025. That gives a conservative 0.19x Debt-to-Equity ratio and backs GNA's `[ICRA]AA- (Stable)` rating [1][5].

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY15–Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Net worth has compounded to ₹1,074 Cr with zero dilutive equity raises since the 2016 IPO, while borrowings declined to ₹203 Cr by Sep 2026 [1].

web_blocks.html: Now let us test earnings quality by comparing Operating Cash Flow (CFO) against EBITDA and Capex. Across FY16–FY26, GNA posted positive CFO in ten out of eleven years. Only FY17 was negative at -₹90 Cr during post-IPO working-capital expansion [1]. From FY18 through FY26, GNA generated ₹834 Cr of cumulative CFO against ₹784 Cr of Net Profit (matching the sum of annual P&L rows). That is a healthy ~106% CFO-to-PAT conversion. Free Cash Flow tells a tighter story, though. GNA spent ₹28–155 Cr a year on fixed assets, so cumulative FCF over FY18–FY26 was modest (~₹38 Cr total, with FY26 adding +₹56 Cr) [1]. Also, FY26 CFO and FCF (₹214 Cr / +₹56 Cr) benefited from Days Payable stretching +53 days (76d to 129d) rather than structural receivable collection [1]. Growth in heavy forging is capital-hungry.

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY15–FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cumulative CFO tracks reported PAT (~106% conversion over FY18–FY26 against ₹784 Cr cumulative Net Profit), but FY26 FCF (+₹56 Cr) benefited from +53d payable stretching (76d→129d) and continuous ₹80–155 Cr annual capex [1].

web_blocks.title: Working Capital Ratios & The ROCE Ceiling

web_blocks.html: The Ratios table below explains why GNA earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality verdict rather than a compounder badge. Over the past decade, ROCE stayed in a 14% to 21% corridor. It sat at 14.3% in FY26, with ROE at 12.2% [1]. Why can't a company with 16% OPM and low debt break above 22%–25% ROCE? Look at working capital: Debtor Days rose from 116–130 days (FY16–FY19) to 151 days in FY25 and FY26. That pushed Cash Conversion Cycle to 139 days and Working Capital Days to 133 days [1]. Note that Q2 FY27 DSO and Maninder Singh Seehra's rationale for his 9.96 pp promoter-group stake sale are not disclosed in public filings [1][4][12]. Giving five months of credit to global OEMs locks up capital that would otherwise compound returns. On ₹1,778 Cr of TTM sales, cutting debtor days by just 20 days would free up nearly ₹97 Cr in cash [1]. That single shift would pay down almost half of GNA's ₹203 Cr debt [1]. Until that collection cycle tightens, capital intensity keeps returns in the mid-teens.

web_blocks.caption: GNA Axles Limited: Working Capital & Capital Efficiency Ratios (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: 151 Debtor Days and 133 Working Capital Days cap GNA's ROCE at 14%–21% (14.3% in FY26; ROE 12.2%), making valuation discipline critical in Pass 2 [1].

book_paragraphs: Every forensic review ends with one question: does the accounting profit turn into spendable cash, and at what return on capital? Let us open GNA Axles' ten-year books from FY15 to FY26 and follow the cash rupee by rupee [1].

On the surface, the P&L is remarkably resilient. Revenue expanded from ₹430 Cr in FY15 to ₹1,478 Cr in FY26—and ₹1,778 Cr on a trailing-twelve-month basis through September 2026—while operating margins never fell below 13% even during COVID or the 2024 US freight slump [1]. Better still, GNA did not dilute shareholders to fund that growth: reserves swelled from ₹98 Cr to ₹1,031 Cr purely through retained earnings, with the FY24 equity jump reflecting a 1:1 bonus issue [1][25]. Total borrowings sit at a modest ₹203 Cr against ₹1,074 Cr of equity [1].

When you check the Cash Flow Statement, earnings quality passes the first test: over the nine years from FY18 through FY26, cumulative Cash Flow from Operations totaled ₹834 Cr against ₹784 Cr of Net Profit—meaning profits are real, not paper accruals [1]. Yet Free Cash Flow tells a more sobering story: FY26 CFO (₹214 Cr) and FCF (+₹56 Cr) benefited from Days Payable stretching +53 days (from 76d to 129d), and because forging presses, induction-hardening lines, and CNC cells require constant reinvestment (₹111 Cr investing outflow in FY25 and ₹155 Cr in FY26), most of GNA's operating cash goes right back into the factory floor [1].

Finally, look at the Ratios table to understand GNA's structural ceiling. Across ten years, ROCE has hovered between 14% and 21%, finishing FY26 at 14.3% with ROE at 12.2% [1]. The culprit is right there in plain sight: 151 Debtor Days and 133 Working Capital Days [1]. Note also that Q2 FY27 DSO and Maninder Singh Seehra's rationale for the 9.96 pp promoter-group stake sale are not disclosed in public filings [1][4][12]. Until GNA either compresses its five-month export collection cycle or shifts materially into higher-margin SUV and EV-allied shafts, it remains a well-run, creditworthy cyclical manufacturer—not a high-ROCE capital-light compounder. That locked business reality sets our exact baseline before we unlock a single stock price in Pass 2.

book_subsections.title: Why 151 Debtor Days Cap ROCE in the 14%–21% Corridor
paragraphs: Look closely at the ten-year capital efficiency math: GNA Axles earned 15%–21% ROCE during the FY18–FY19 and FY23 booms, and 14%–15% during the FY20–FY21 and FY24–FY26 slowdowns (14.3% ROCE and 12.2% ROE in FY26) [1]. Why doesn't a company with 16% operating margins and ₹203 Cr of low-cost debt compound at 25%+ ROCE? Because 151 Debtor Days and 117 Inventory Days tie up ₹1,213 Cr of Other Assets (largely receivables and inventory) alongside ₹516 Cr of Fixed Assets and CWIP [1]. Until GNA compresses its five-month export collection cycle or shifts decisively into higher-margin machined SUV/EV shafts, its intrinsic business quality is squarely CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL—creditworthy, cash-generative over a full cycle, and resilient, but capital-intensive.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Locking the Price-Blind Verdict Before Looking at the Tape
book_callouts.text: We have now completed our entire price-blind audit of GNA Axles without looking at a single stock price or P/E multiple. Here is what we know with certainty: GNA is a [ICRA]AA- Tier-1 specialist with real OEM qualification moats, a sharp H1 FY27 revenue rebound (+37% Q1, +50% Q2), low debt, and disciplined 13%–16% margins [1][3][4][5]. At the same time, its 14.3% ROCE, 12.2% ROE, 151 debtor days, 80% top-10 customer concentration, and recent promoter-group stake reduction place it squarely in CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL territory [1][5][12]. In Pass 2, we will test whether the market is pricing GNA as a cyclical or a compounder.
